written_before: any full run; smokes may revise designs, revisions dated in 'revisions'
format: prediction id: [statement, my probability]; verdict bands are the ones coded in each script

e680_floor_causal.question: is the extreme-value floor a causal boundary for the model's own readers?
C1: at 0.5 floors, own and foreign native injections cost the same next-token KL as a random direction (ratio in [0.7, 1.5])
C2: at 2 floors, the position's own write scaled up costs more than 2x a random direction
C3: at 2 floors, a foreign native row costs the same as a random direction (e510/e511: a fake chord is contracted like noise)
C4: the rotated row equals random at every amplitude

e681_weak_ablation.question: do weak activations matter, and to whom?
W1: keeping only the strongest quarter of each neuron's activations by count (the essay's vision measure) costs under 0.05 nats of KL
W2: the dial tertile (lowest top-1% energy share) costs at least twice the detector tertile
W3: flipped predictions were near-ties: their clean margin's median is under half the unflipped median
W4: the last block costs at least twice the average block per neuron
W5: mean replacement is cheaper than zeroing
W1c: zeroing activations below 0.1 of each neuron's maximum (the first form of W1) costs under 0.05 nats

e682_fact_map.question: are a learned fact's writers related to the fact, or an arbitrary store?
F1: at least half of a fact's sixteen writers fire on natural Pile text about its value or relation (z > 3)
F2: facts sharing a value share writers more than twice as much (Jaccard) as facts of different relations
F3: the random codes' writers are related to a code-like field at most half as often as facts' writers to theirs
F3b: the codes share writers among themselves at least as much as facts of one relation do (packing)
F4: the writers' median depth is in the last third
F5: no write column changes by more than 0.02 in cosine (existing routes, no rewritten row)

e683_chain_star.question: chain, star or jump: the topology of a neuron's growth over training
G1: chain enrichment (new contexts nearest a member that entered within two checkpoints, over the random expectation) exceeds 1.5 in at least 70% of neurons
G2: the median jump share (nearest member below the random-position null) is under 0.15
G3: the root (top-20 at step 1000) is more one-token concentrated than the final top-20
G4: in two-route neurons the minor route's members entered by chain more often than the core's, in at least 60%

e684_readers.question: do downstream readers arrive after a row is recruited (buildability)?
R1: the recruited row gains readers (|share| > 1 std) from two checkpoints before to two after, more than norm-matched control rows on the same positions, in at least 65% of words
R2: the readers' alignment gain with the row exceeds their gain with the class direction in at least 60%
R3: sub-class specialists among later-block neurons increase across recruitment more than for random position sets in at least 60%
R1b: the ten strongest readers' mean share gains more across recruitment than the norm-matched control rows' on the same positions, in at least 65% of words
R1c: the total reader mass gains more than the control rows' in at least 65% of words

e685_readers_ledger.question: how many upstream inputs does a neuron need; readable writes or the crowd?
L1: the K=16 simulation's KL ratio is lower at the neuron's strong positions than over all positions
L2_nick: at K=16 the median KL ratio at strong positions is under 0.25
L3: over-floor upstream writes carry more than half of the MLP input energy at strong firings
L0: driven by every input, the simulated neuron reproduces the model (KL ratio under 0.05): a check of the exact split

e686_negative_pole.question: is the negative pole the nearest neighbour?
N1: at the middle block, more than half of neurons have pole-state cosine above the null's 95th percentile (read axes projected out)
N2: the near share rises with depth
N3: next-token overlap between poles beats the null for more than 0.3 of neurons

e687_explanation_recall.question: how compact and how complete is a surface explanation of a neuron's class?
X1_gao: median held-out precision at recall 0.9 is under 0.3 at the middle block
X2_gao: a rule reaching recall 0.9 at precision 0.5 exists for under half, or its median size exceeds 50 entries
X2_nick: such a rule has at most 10 entries for at least half
X3: a surface rule at precision 0.5 covers at least half of a neuron's held-out class at the middle block

e688_plant_knot.question: is arbitrary packing an unstable state (semantic gravity)?
K1: both concepts install at the pin's end (vote share at least 0.8 each) in at least 4 of 5 seeds
K2_gravity: by release step 6000 at least one vote share falls below 0.5 in at least 3 of 5 seeds
K2_stable: both stay at least 0.8 in at least 3 of 5 seeds
K3: single-concept pins keep vote share at least 0.8 through release in at least 3 of 4 runs
K4: a shed concept's dial is under 0.03 (dials follow votes)

e689_width.question: do readable writes grow and the crowd shrink with width?
S1: rows over the floor per position grow with d within each family (Spearman > 0.8)
S2: the crowd share of the resultant falls with d (Spearman < -0.5 within families)
S3: the effective number of contributors to the resultant grows with d (Spearman > 0.5)

e690_memorized.question: are memorised sequences' writers late, coherent and content-related?
M1: memorised writers sit more than one block deeper than both controls
M2: their class entropy is not higher than the controls' (within 0.2 bits)
M3: the share firing on the content field is not lower than the low-loss control's

e691_reader_consensus.question: does the activation label agree with what readers do?
C1: Spearman over pairs between token-bag similarity and reader-vector similarity exceeds 0.3
C2: a neuron's nearest neighbour by tokens is among its ten nearest by readers for more than 0.3 (chance 0.01)
C3: weight-only reader vectors correlate with ledger reader vectors above 0.5

revisions: 2026-10-18 after the smokes, before any full run: e681 gained the keep-top-q conditions (W1 restated on the strongest quarter kept, the fraction-of-max form kept as W1c) because a tenth of the maximum removes a third of Pythia's activation energy; e686's null became the two tails of a rotated read row (projecting out the read axis left residual anti-correlation); e687 gained graded precision and recall points (X3) because precision at recall 0.9 saturates at zero; e684's reader threshold went from one std (nobody) to a fifth, with the ten strongest readers' share and the mass as R1b and R1c; e685 gained K = 256, 1024 and all inputs (L0) and the fp32 log-probs; e691's reader signature became the causal downstream response (the ledger-weighted one was the weight vector times a scalar); c11 stored clean log-probs in fp32 (fp16 put a 1e-3-nat floor under every KL).

2026-10-18 during the full runs: e684 keeps its activation cache in CPU RAM (an OOM on seed 0, rerun); e690 keeps its reference activations in CPU RAM (OOMs on 410m and 1B, rerun); e682 gained a KL tether to the base model (beta 2) and lr 5e-6 after the first Pythia-410m run damaged the model by 0.87 nats, and skips reference sentences under four tokens (a crash); e685b (the crowd's mean added back) was written after e685's first results showed the K-input simulation worse than ablation at mid depth, as the error-node control; the verdict bands coded in the scripts are the ones above.

e685b_crowdmean.question: e685's control: the K largest inputs plus the corpus mean of what they leave out (the crowd replaced by its mean, the error-node convention)
L0: every input reproduces the neuron (KL ratio under 0.05)
L4: adding the crowd's mean halves the K=16 KL ratio at strong positions
L5: with the crowd's mean the K=16 ratio at strong positions is under 0.25
L6: with the crowd's mean the K=64 ratio is under 0.25
